newsitem.title: THAILAND: Corporate tax cuts seen boosting Thai economy.
newsitem.headline: Corporate tax cuts seen boosting Thai economy.

text.p: Corporate tax cuts will provide a major stimulus to the Thai economy, the Thai Farmers Research Centre said on Wednesday.

"In order to stimulate the economy so that it would induce more foreign direct investment inflows into the Thai economy, corporate income tax should be urgently reduced," Thai Farmers said in a report.
Economic recovery could only be achieved through fiscal reductions, since the impact of applicable monetary measures would be slight, it said.
A corporate tax cut is one proposal being studied by the Thai Finance Ministry but a decision on any cut is unlikely to be made prior to a November 17 general election.

"At present, with the economy in recession, fiscal policies, particularly the reduction of the corporate income tax rate, should be a more appropriate measure to stimulate the economy," Thai Farmers said. "For the new government the corporate income tax cut should be considered a priority."

Thai Farmers said a three percent cut in corporate income tax would increase gross domestic product, investment, increase exports, boost employment, decrease inflation and improve the balance of trade.
In Thailand, corporate tax is 30 percent. By comparison, rates in Singapore are around 26 percent.
According to most private estimates, Thailand's gross domestic product is set to grow by less than seven percent this year, down from 8.6 percent in 1995.
